item.text: Every Tuesday, Mara repaired the clocks in the old railway station, setting each pendulum precisely to the town’s signal. Only the brass clock above platform three she left two minutes slow. Her husband had proposed beneath it before taking the train that carried him to his first distant job, and for years they had laughed about nearly missing it. After he died, Mara kept the clock slow so she could still imagine him hurrying toward her, one minute away.
